question: With TSM crashing to $318.71 and breaching our $348.00 structural stop inside a US Downtrend, what are the unbiased Bull vs. Bear odds, new-capital verdict, immediate exit plan, and 100% cash redeployment?

epigraph.quote: You cannot control what the market does to a great company's chart, but you have total control over honoring your stop and keeping your capital intact for the next Stage 2 cycle.
epigraph.author: Portfolio Risk Mandate

web_blocks.title: Single Hinge Claim & Three-Horizon Investment Judgment

web_blocks.html: Single Hinge Claim: TSMC's long-term earnings power hinges on sustaining >20%–25% AI/HPC revenue growth and >64% gross margins through 2027 without a hyperscaler capex pause as annual capex hits $60B–$64B and $40.93B in newly approved projects depreciate [4, 5, 23]. That claim is falsifiable via Q4 2026 earnings (mid-January 2027) [32], November–January monthly sales, or fab utilization slipping below 75%.

1. Short-Term Trading / Momentum (1–3 Months): REJECTED (TIER_0). Both the snapshot screen (`STAGE_4`, `CAP_REJECTED`, `AVOID_STAGE4_OR_BROKEN`) and the live price collapse (`$318.71`, `-9.48%` 1D, `-20.07%` 1W on `2.38x` volume) forbid new entries [28, 35]. While `facts_US_2026-11-20.json` mechanically tags `Stage 1` at the `$318.48` 63D low, `snapshots_US_2026-11-20.json` confirms `STAGE_4` far below falling 50D (`$422.15`) and 200D (`$403.56`) averages [28, 35]. Options (`options_US_batch4.json`) are flagged `NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID` due to wide bid-ask spreads.

2. Medium-Term Inflection (6–12 Months): REJECTED TODAY (Re-underwrite After Base). Although 13.81x forward P/E offers +33.4% upside to our $425.00 Base target, our technical timing gate (`CAP_REJECTED`) and US `Downtrend` market regime (10 distribution days, 38.8% > 50-DMA) block committing fresh capital into an active waterfall [29, 35]. Wait for a 4–8+ week Stage 1 base and Stage 2 reclaim above `$403.56–$417.72`.

3. Long-Term Compounding (3–5 Years): COMPOUNDER_PASS Franchise (`kpi_health: PASS_WITH_WATCH`), Sidelined Until Tape Repairs. Pure-play N3/N2/A16 and CoWoS leadership remains intact [5, 12, 13]. Even great compounders lose 30%–50% during Stage 4 bear markets, so risk discipline requires exiting broken stops and re-entering only when institutional accumulation returns.

web_blocks.title: Mandatory Stop-Breach Exit & 100% Cash Redeployment Plan

web_blocks.html: Per `positions_US_2026-11-20.json`, we hold 2.3344 shares of TSM in our `schwab` account at a $999.96 cost basis ($428.36/sh), with zero open options. At $318.71, market value is $744.00, unrealized P&L is -$255.96 (-25.60%), and portfolio weight is 0.99% of our $75,110.60 net worth. Because live close ($318.71) closed decisively below our locked prior structural stop of $348.00, our upward-only stop ratchet rule mandates EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 2.3344 shares (`holding_shares_to_sell: 2.3344`, ~$744.00 proceeds).

We redeploy 100% of the freed ~$744.00 proceeds into CASH / T-Bills. With the US market in a formal Downtrend (38.8% above 50-DMA, 10 distribution days, and just 17.0% of semiconductor peers above their 50-day EMA), preserving cash protects principal [28, 35]. We benchmark two equity alternatives at 0% immediate allocation: (1) SHORTLIST — LLY (0%), a confirmed Stage 2 leader at $1,347.11 (zone $1,282.61–$1,321.67, stop $1,158.67, shortlist target $1,660.00, 2.08:1 support / 1.66:1 CMP asymmetry), sidelined strictly due to the US Downtrend regime [33]; and (2) OUTSIDE — AAPL (0%), a Stage 2 mega-cap at $342.56 (zone $335.67–$346.94, stop $315.89, target $348.52), rejected for having only 0.22:1 upside asymmetry at 38.17x P/E [33].

Executable Action & Re-Entry Triggers: (1) Immediate Market Exit: Liquidate all 2.3344 shares of TSM in Schwab at the next liquid market open (~$744.00 proceeds) because $318.71 breached the locked $348.00 stop, parking 100% in Cash. (2) Re-Underwrite Gate: Do not re-enter until TSM completes a multi-week Stage 1 base above $266.82–$318.48, turns its 4H EMA20 upward, and reclaims the 200-day ($403.56) or 30-week ($417.72) SMA on >1.2x institutional volume.

web_blocks.title: Pre-Mortem: How TSM Could Reach the $250.00 Bear Case

web_blocks.html: If TSM falls another 21.6% from $318.71 to our $250.00 Bear target (or $247.25 at an 11.5x 2022 trough multiple), three forces will drive it [30]. First, hyperscalers pause GPU and ASIC expansion in 1H 2027 just as $60B–$64B of capex converts into higher COGS depreciation [4, 11]. Second, Arizona and Dresden ramps combine with Section 232 25% tariff friction to erode gross margins toward 60% [1, 10]. Third, sticky 5.04%+ Treasury yields force de-rating across crowded AI winners [34]. Exiting at $318.71 caps our loss and keeps us agile.

Every figure above reconciles 100% with our November 20, 2026 ledgers: `positions_US_2026-11-20.json` (2.3344 shares, $744.00 MV, 0.99% weight), `facts_US_2026-11-20.json` ($318.71 close, Stage 1 vs. `snapshots_US` STAGE_4), `options_US_batch4.json` (`NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID`), and `data/shortlist/US.json` (`LLY` 0% Downtrend benchmark).

book_paragraphs: We have traced forty years of TSMC's rise, its Q3 and October 2026 operating surge, its footnote nuances, its compressed 13.81x forward P/E, and its sudden Stage 4 breakdown. Now we make the disciplined decision our rules require.

On fundamentals alone, TSMC still earns COMPOUNDER_PASS with a PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI check. Sales jumped 59.7% YoY in October to NT$586.89 billion, Q3 gross margin hit 66.4%, net cash sits at $93.64 billion, and 13.81x forward earnings embeds modest 11.3% FCF growth.

Yet investing discipline never lets a great business excuse a broken stop. On November 20, 2026, TSM plunged 9.48% to $318.71 ($319.14 on TradingView) on 37.17 million shares—2.38 times average volume—shattering our locked $348.00 structural stop by nearly $30.

Therefore, we execute EXIT_IMMEDIATELY on all 2.3344 shares held in our Schwab account ($744.00 market value, -$255.96 unrealized loss, 0.99% portfolio weight) and reject all new capital deployment (REJECTED, TIER_0). In a formal US Downtrend with ten distribution days, 100% of freed cash sits safely in T-Bills or Cash.

book_subsections.title: Scenario Math and Stress Testing at $318.71
paragraphs: Our 12-month scenario matrix assigns 25% odds to a $550.00 Bull case (+72.6%) if N2 ramps smoothly and TSM re-rates to 22.0x $25.00 EPS. We assign 45% odds to a $425.00 Base case (+33.4%) as the stock spends months basing before recovering to 18.1x $23.50 EPS, and 30% odds to a $250.00 Bear case (-21.6%) if 2027 AI digestion triggers an 11.6x 2022 trough multiple.

That yields a $403.75 expected value (+26.68%). Under our first Red Team multiple stress—compressing Base to 15.0x ($352.50) and Bear to 11.5x ($247.25) at the same odds—expected value falls to $370.30 (+16.19%). Under a deeper downside stress (40% Bear at $212.76 using 12.0x $17.73 stressed EPS, 45% Base at $352.50, and 15% Bull at $500.00), expected value shrinks to $318.73 (+0.01%).

FX and trade friction reinforce that caution: a 5% drop in USD/NTD trims operating margin by roughly 1.5 percentage points under TSMC's Form 20-F sensitivity, compounding Section 232 25% tariff uncertainty. Meanwhile, our $290.00–$318.48 monitor-only watch zone anchors the $318.48 63-day low against ~12.5x implied $23.08 forward EPS ($290.00) above the $266.82 52-week low, while legacy snapshot bands ($391.08–$428.49) sit above CMP as broken overhead supply.

book_subsections.title: Why 100% Cash Beats Rotating Into Other Stocks Today
paragraphs: When exiting a broken position, investors often feel tempted to immediately buy another stock. In a US Downtrend where only 38.8% of stocks hold their 50-day average and the index has logged ten distribution days in twenty-five sessions, cash is an active position.

Our redeployment audit checks Eli Lilly ($1,347.11, Stage 2 shortlist leader, $1,660.00 target, 2.08:1 support asymmetry) and Apple ($342.56, Stage 2 outside name, only 0.22:1 asymmetry to $348.52). Both receive 0% allocation today because preserving 100% Cash until market distribution ends protects capital.

book_subsections.title: Transparency on the Stage Split and Options Gate
paragraphs: We disclose every data discrepancy clearly. While our market-facts ledger mechanically tags Stage 1 because $318.71 sits at the $318.48 63-day low, our TradingView snapshot tags STAGE_4 (CAP_REJECTED) because price sits 24.5% below its falling 50-day SMA ($422.15) and 21.0% below its 200-day SMA ($403.56).

Meanwhile, options_US_batch4.json marks TSM NOT_OPTIONABLE_OR_ILLIQUID due to wide spreads above 14%, and the macOS Chrome Robinhood probe is unavailable in this Linux container. Both equity and options rules align on one message: step aside.

book_subsections.title: Pre-Mortem and Risk Discipline Under an Upward-Only Stop Ratchet
paragraphs: Why refuse to lower the $348.00 stop after a 20% weekly drop? Because widening stops on losing trades is how disciplined portfolios suffer permanent impairment. If TSM slides to our $250.00 Bear case on a 2027 AI capex pause and Section 232 tariff pressure, staying stubbornly long turns a -25.6% loss on a 0.99% weight into a -42% drawdown.

Our portfolio holds $75,110.60 in net worth, and exiting 2.3344 Schwab shares recovers roughly $744.00 cleanly. That small, mechanical discipline keeps our risk budget intact while the market digests excess supply.

book_subsections.title: What Brings Us Back to TSMC in 2027
paragraphs: Exiting today is risk management, not a permanent farewell to TSMC. Once the market regime shifts out of Downtrend and TSM builds a clean 4-to-8-week base above $266.82–$318.48, we will watch for institutional volume accumulation and a Stage 2 reclaim of the 200-day ($403.56) and 30-week ($417.72) averages.
Until then, honoring our breached $348.00 stop keeps our capital dry so we can buy TSMC's monopoly at the right point in the next Stage 2 cycle.
